articles.name: Announcing browser multi-tab support for Contact Center
articles.title: Announcing browser multi-tab support for Contact Center
articles.body:
We’re happy to announce that native Zendesk Contact Center now includes enhanced multi-tab support to prevent duplicate tickets when agents work across multiple browser tabs or windows. This improvement ensures that each customer call creates exactly one ticket, eliminating confusion and improving data accuracy, without changing how your agents work.

This article includes the following sections:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Contact Center now creates tickets on the backend server instead of in each browser tab. When your agents have multiple tabs open, an incoming call rings and displays in each tab, but Contact Center creates only one ticket for the call.

Note: This change affects only how Contact Center creates tickets. It does not change call routing, agent availability, call handling, or existing Contact Center configuration.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Previously, when agents had multiple browser tabs or windows open, Contact Center created a separate ticket in each tab for the same call. This resulted in:

  • Duplicate tickets appearing in queues for the same customer interaction.
  • Agent confusion about which ticket to use.
  • Data inconsistencies affecting reporting and analytics.

This improvement eliminates these issues by ensuring every call creates exactly one ticket, regardless of how many tabs your agents have open. Your data will be cleaner, your reports more accurate, and your agents can work more efficiently.

What do I need to do?

No action is required. This change will roll out gradually to all native Zendesk Contact Center customers by the end of August 2026. Once enabled for your account, the improvement will be active immediately with no configuration needed.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Announcing more control over agent status updates from external site visits
articles.title: Announcing more control over agent status updates from external site visits
articles.body:
We’re excited to announce the general availability of new controls in Zendesk Workforce Management (WFM) for automatic agent status updates when agents visit external sites.

A new Update agent status setting on the extension tracking configuration page lets admins control which tracked activities trigger automatic status updates.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Previously, when the Zendesk WFM Chrome extension started an activity from a configured URL mapping, it automatically updated the agent’s status to the status associated with that mapping.

With these controls, admins can choose when activities tracked by the Zendesk WFM Chrome extension update an agent’s status in Zendesk Support. This provides greater flexibility for organizations that want to track agent activity while retaining control over how and when agent statuses change.

Key highlights:

  • Existing behavior is preserved: Automatic status updates are enabled by default, so existing configurations continue to work without any action from admins.
  • Global control: Admins can turn automatic status updates on or off for Extension Tracking.
  • Flexible configuration: Admins can apply automatic status updates to all mappings, selected mappings only, or configured unmapped URLs.
  • Per-mapping control: When using selected mappings, admins can choose which individual URL mappings update agent status.
  • Bulk management: Admins can enable or disable automatic status updates for multiple mappings at once.
  • Tracking-only workflows: When automatic status updates are disabled, the Chrome extension continues to track the agent activity without changing the agent’s status in Support.
  • Configuration is preserved: If admins disable and later re-enable automatic status updates, previously selected mapping settings remain intact.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Customers asked for more flexibility in how Extension Tracking interacts with agent statuses. Although automatic status updates support many workflows, some organizations need to manage agent availability manually or update statuses only for specific activities.

With these new controls:

  • Admins can align extension tracking with their organization’s existing operational workflows.
  • Agents’ activity can be tracked without unintended changes to their availability.
  • Organizations can choose which activities should affect an agent’s status.
  • WFM teams can use extension tracking to monitor activity without automating status updates.
  • Fewer unnecessary status update requests are sent when automatic updates aren’t needed.

What do I need to do?

No action is required. This feature is automatically available to all Zendesk WFM customers who use the Zendesk time tracker extension. The Update agent status setting is enabled by default, and existing URL mappings will continue to update agent statuses automatically.

To learn how to install the extension and customize automatic status updates, see Tracking agent time spent outside of Zendesk.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum, where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Announcing templated opening and closing email responses for AI agents with agentic AI
articles.title: Announcing templated opening and closing email responses for AI agents with agentic AI
articles.body:
We're excited to announce the ability to configure your own opening and closing lines for email AI agents with agentic AI.

This announcement answers the following questions:

  • What's changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What's changing?

Admins can now define their own opening and closing lines for the emails their AI agents send with agentic AI, instead of relying on AI-generated text. Previously, these email AI agents used generative AI to compose the opening and closing lines of every email reply—for example, "Good morning," or "Best regards,". These lines couldn't be edited, so the greeting and sign-off varied from reply to reply.

With this update, a new Email content page in your AI agent's configuration lets you set a static opening line and closing line. You can personalize the greeting with the requester's name (for example, "Dear <customer name>,"), and you can define separate templates for each language your AI agent is configured to support.

If you don't configure a template, nothing changes: your AI agent continues to generate opening and closing lines as it does today.

Note the following limitations for this release:

  • The email footer remains static and can't be edited.
  • Templates aren't translated automatically. You provide your own version of each template for every language you support.
  • Templates are fixed strings. The AI agent doesn't adjust their grammar, so languages with gender- or case-sensitive forms (such as the vocative case in Polish) may need wording that avoids inflected names.

For more information, see Configuring an AI agent’s opening and closing lines in email responses.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

We've heard your feedback that you want direct control over how your AI agents open and close emails. Your feedback pointed to three gaps:

  • Personalization: You want to greet end users by name rather than with a generic, time-based greeting.
  • Brand consistency: Businesses have specific sign-off styles and tone needs that generated text doesn't reliably match.
  • Predictability: Admins want the same opening and closing lines on every reply, not variable output.

Making opening and closing lines configurable puts control in your hands, in the same place you configure the rest of your AI agent.

What do I need to do?

No action is required. Email templates are automatically available to all accounts using email AI agents with agentic AI starting August 25, 2026. 

Your AI agents continue to generate opening and closing lines until you configure templates of your own. When you're ready to customize them, see Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines in email responses
articles.title: Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines in email responses
articles.body:
You can customize opening and closing lines for your AI agent's email responses. The customized text is sent exactly as written. It isn't generated, translated, or modified by the AI agent, and it isn't affected by the AI agent'sinstructionsor otherpersonalization settings, including tone of voice or pronoun formality.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise
This article applies only to email AI agents with agentic AI.

You can customize opening and closing lines for your AI agent's email responses. The customized text is sent exactly as written. It isn't generated, translated, or modified by the AI agent, and it isn't affected by the AI agent's instructions or other personalization settings, including tone of voice or pronoun formality.

If you don’t customize specific opening and closing lines, the AI agent uses AI-generated text for its openings and closings.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines
  • Using AI-generated opening and closing lines

Customizing an AI agent’s opening and closing lines

You can customize the opening and closing lines of email responses by creating templates for each language you support.

Keep the following limitations in mind:

  • The email footer remains static and can't be edited.
  • Templates aren't translated automatically. You provide your own version of each template for every language you support.
  • Templates are fixed strings. The AI agent doesn't adjust their grammar, so languages with gender- or case-sensitive forms (such as the vocative case in Polish) may need wording that avoids inflected names.

To customize an AI agent's email opening and closing lines

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Email content.
  3. Click Manage languages in the upper-right to select one of the supported languages you’ve added.
  4. Click Opening line and enter the text the AI agent should use at the beginning of each email response.

    Optionally, you can personalize the text with the customer’s name. Place the cursor where you want to insert the name, type a forward slash (/), and select one of the following options:

    • customerFirstName
    • customerLastName
    • customerFullName

    Note: If your AI agent was created before July 30, 2026, see Populating the customer name variables for an additional step required to use the customer name variables listed above.
    Alternatively, leave the field empty to use an AI-generated opening line.
  5. Click Closing line and enter the text the AI agent should use at the end of each email response.

    Optionally, you can personalize the text with the customer’s name, as described above.

    Alternatively, leave the field empty to use an AI-generated opening line.
  6. Click Save.
  7. In the Languages panel, click the options menu () for the language you’re customizing and select Enable.

Using AI-generated opening and closing lines

You can configure your AI agent to use AI-generated opening and closing lines, instead of specifically customized ones.

You can do this by leaving the fields blank when you customize the opening and closing lines, or by disabling opening and closing line customizations for a language altogether.

You can disable customizations for a language only if you’ve previously enabled them.

To disable opening and closing customizations

  1. In the AI agents workspace, select the AI agent you want to work with.
  2. Click Content in the sidebar, then select Email content.
  3. Click Manage languages in the upper-right to select one of the supported languages you’ve added.
  4. Click the options menu () for the language you want to disable opening and closing customizations for, then select Disable.

Issue symptoms

In my AI agent, I tried to add the link to my website under external content sources or external connections. However, the status of my website shows as Blocked.

Resolution steps

    • Shop is a free Zendesk help center theme for retail. Shop gives ecommerce brands, retailers, and consumer marketplaces a clean, fast Guide theme, with every color, font, and layout option customizable from Theming Center, no code required.

    • Stack is a free Zendesk help center theme for software and cloud services. Stack gives SaaS companies, developer tools, and cloud platforms a clean, technical Guide theme, with every color, font, and layout option customizable from Theming Center, no code required.

    • Signal is a free Zendesk help center theme for telecommunications. Signal gives mobile carriers, internet providers, and connectivity platforms a bright, reassuring Guide theme, with every color, font, and layout option customizable from Theming Center, no code required.

    • Forge is a free Zendesk help center theme for manufacturing. Forge gives equipment makers, industrial suppliers, and parts distributors a rugged, high-contrast Guide theme, with every color, font, and layout option customizable from Theming Center, no code required.

    • Cast is a free Zendesk help center theme for media. Cast gives streaming services, publishers, and audio platforms a bold, editorial Guide theme, with every color, font, and layout option customizable from Theming Center, no code required. 
  • Improvado (Support)
    • Improvado is an AI-powered marketing intelligence platform for enterprise marketing, revenue, and support teams. It connects 500+ data sources, automates data preparation, and delivers analytics-ready data to your data warehouse and BI tools. Extract tickets, users, and ticket fields from the Zendesk REST API v2, on a schedule you control. Data is transferred over TLS and delivered to the customer's own Improvado workspace and data warehouse, and is used only to produce that customer's analytics.
  • Recurring Tickets by Veryation (Support) (paid)
    • Recurring Tickets by Veryation puts routine work on autopilot. Define a ticket once — subject, description, requester, assignee group, priority, type, and tags — choose a schedule, and it creates that ticket automatically every time it falls due. It is built for work that happens on a cadence: preventative maintenance, compliance and audit evidence, periodic access reviews, recurring reports, and follow-ups nobody can afford to forget.

    • Gatekeeper Bot automatically collects customer information before routing conversations to your agents — so every ticket arrives with the right fields already filled in. The bot engages customers in natural dialogue, asking questions one at a time in the customer’s own language. A structured form is delivered inside the messaging channel. Ideal for straightforward intake flows or when you prefer not to use AI.
  • Asyntai AI Agent (Support)
    • Asyntai AI Agent adds an AI customer support agent to your Zendesk Messaging channels. Once installed, the bot answers your customers' questions instantly — 24/7, in 36 languages, automatically detected from the customer's message. The AI uses your own website content, FAQs, and product information to give answers that actually reflect your business — not generic responses. Conversations carry context, so follow-up questions are handled naturally.

articles.name: Why can’t I find tickets when searching a numeric custom field with a very large value?
articles.title: Why can’t I find tickets when searching a numeric custom field with a very large value?
articles.body:
Question

Why search does not return expected results when I search using a very large value in a numeric custom ticket field?

Answer

Zendesk search supports numeric custom field values only within the following range:

  • -9,223,372,036,854,775,808 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807

If a numeric field contains a value outside this range, search for that value may not return expected ticket results.

This limit is a numeric value limit, not a character limit. This behavior is due to a limitation of the search backend.

For example, if you need to store and search identifiers larger than this range, consider a text field instead of a numeric field.

Use numeric fields for values that fit within the supported 64-bit signed integer range. Use text fields for very large numeric identifiers that you must search.

To learn more about searching for tickets, see Searching Zendesk Support data.

articles.name: Understanding advanced action flows (EAP)
articles.title: Understanding advanced action flows (EAP)
articles.body:
Advanced action flows provide a more powerful way to build automation for service by supporting workflows that can branch, pause for human input, connect across systems, and adapt as business rules evolve. This allows teams to automate more of their work, reducing manual effort and increasing scalability and control.

What's my plan?
All Suites Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

Advanced action flows let you automate complex, long-running workflows with branching, pauses, and integrations across many systems using code. They support custom API calls, detailed error tracking, version control, and reuse across workflows. Use them for workflows needing complex logic, human approvals, or attachment processing. They run in secure sandboxes with execution limits and require authentication for external APIs.

Advanced action flows provide a more powerful way to build automation for service by supporting workflows that can branch, pause for human input, connect across systems, and adapt as business rules evolve. This allows teams to automate more of their work, reducing manual effort and increasing scalability and control.

This article contains the following topics:
  • Understanding the difference between action flows and advanced action flows
  • Choosing the best automated workflow for your use cases
  • Essential facts about advanced action flows
Related articles
  • Creating advanced action flows
  • Advanced action flows API reference
  • Editing and managing advanced action flows
  • Monitoring and troubleshooting advanced action flows

Understanding the difference between action flows and advanced action flows

Action flows and advanced action flows both address the same class of use case: automated sequences of steps that can perform actions in Zendesk and external systems. In general, action flows are best for no or low-code repeatable automated workflows that are simple or moderately complex, while advanced action flows are code-based and designed for more complex and variable workflows.

The following table provides an in-depth comparison of action flows and advanced action flows:
  Action flows Advanced action flows
Creation method Drag-and-drop components in visual builder Conversational AI prompt that generates editable code
Visual diagram Built by the user in the action builder Generated based on the code
Complexity Low to medium complexity workflows Low to high complexity workflows
Automation style Structured, repeatable process automation Flexible orchestration to support complex business logic
Extending to new APIs Must be predefined as an action All REST APIs supported
Troubleshooting, drafts, and version control Visual review, testing, and step-based editing. Direct access to code, execution traces, and version history, including visual review of the generated flowchart.
Typical user Admins and process owners who prefer not to write code Technical admins, developers, and process owners
Ownership model Better for broad admin adoption and ease of use Better for precision and control

Choosing the best automated workflow for your use cases

Because action flows and advanced action flows have overlapping capabilities, it's important to understand when they can both accomplish your goals and when one is a better choice over the other.

When to use advanced action flows

Advanced action flows are typically the best choice if your workflow requires:
  • Long-running processes over days or weeks, often with human approval steps in the middle.
  • Complex business logic, such as nested conditions, loops, regular expressions, parsing JSON or custom objects, handling exceptions, or sharing states across steps.
  • Attachment processing, such as reading data out of invoices, IDs, spreadsheets, or archives.
  • Integrations with many systems, particularly internal, legacy, or niche APIs that aren't supported as pre-built connectors for action builder.

Examples that are well-suited to advanced action flows include: dynamic API calls, advanced data transformations, multi-branching logic, and retries.

Other benefits of advanced action flows include:
  • Unlike action flows, you aren't limited to pre-built connectors. Instead, you can use new, internal, or legacy REST API endpoints immediately without having to manually create custom actions. Additionally, every endpoint and parameter the service supports is available for use in your advanced action flows, including endpoints released after your workflow is created.
  • Because advanced action flows call APIs directly, you don't have to maintain connectors.
  • Every time you save an advanced action flow, a version is saved in the version history, making it easy to track changes and revert to an earlier version if necessary. Each advanced action flow has a currently published version as well as read-only snapshots of all prior versions.
  • Every time an advanced action flow runs, every execution records console outputs, network requests and responses, inputs, outputs, and errors. This information makes it possible to quickly identify the problem if failures occur.
  • Advanced action flows have predictable behavior and cost at scale, consuming neither action credits nor model tokens unless you add an AI step.
  • Advanced action flows can be invoked by AI agents and other workflows, making them reusable across the Zendesk platform.
It's also important to understand what you can't do with advanced action flows. You can't:
  • Install or import third-party packages
  • Access the system
  • Open raw sockets
  • Use the following JavaScript features: eval, Proxy, Reflect, WeakMap, WeakSet, WeakRef, SharedArrayBuffer, and WebAssembly
  • Rely on variables after the workflow is paused

If advanced action flows are a good fit for your workflow, see Creating advanced action flows.

When to use action flows

Action flows are typically the best choice if your workflow requires:
  • No code or low-code workflow creation and management.
  • Lower complexity logic for the workflow.
  • Highly repeatable and structured steps that are defined with the supported Zendesk steps and pre-built connector steps.

Examples that are well-suited to action flows include: ticket routing, approvals, status updates, and other standard workflow automations.

For more information, see Creating action flows to automate processes across Zendesk and external systems.

Essential facts about advanced action flows

Consider the following key concepts and details before creating advanced action flows:
  • Advanced action flows consist of the following parts:
    1. Advanced action flow trigger: The condition under which the workflow is initiated. This could be a Zendesk event (ticket, user, organization, asset, or custom object is created, updated, or deleted), a recurring schedule, manual initiation, a webhook called by an external system, or invocation by an AI agent or other workflow.
    2. Actions: Each action is an annotated section of your code that appears as a node in the flowchart and as a boundary in the execution interface.

      Steps can include a Pause, which causes the workflow to stop and wait for a specified duration of time, an event to occur, an approval to be received, or for another workflow to finish.

  • Generally speaking, advanced action flows use AI during the workflow creation process to generate the code and a flowchart, but not when the workflow itself is running.

    However, it is possible to incorporate AI actions into the workflow, in which case AI is used for that process as well. To incorporate AI into your advanced action flows, use the agents.run() call.

  • Advanced action flows run in isolated environments with platform globals instead of Node.js or browser APIs. The isolated environment is referred to as a sandbox. This means there is no file system, raw sockets, or packages to import.
    Each capability your workflow uses, whether that's making an HTTP request, reading a ticket, or storing a value, is a request to the host platform, which validates the request before acting. Several isolation layers sit between your code and Zendesk infrastructure, including separate runner processes, dedicated virtual machine instance per execution with its own memory ceiling, a container with no network egress permitted, and a read-only file system running as a non-privileged user. Because of these precautions, advanced action flows can't reach anything they haven't been explicitly granted access to and can't affect the data or workflows of other accounts.
    Note: The sandboxes used to isolate the advanced action flows are not the same as Zendesk sandboxes, which are used by admins and agents with permission to test features and configurations outside of their production environment.
  • All API calls made by an advanced action flow are attributed to the administrator who created the workflow. This means the workflow has the same permissions and access as the creator and are constrained by your account's normal rate limits. In the code, user.creator identifies the workflow's author and user.runner identifies the user or system that triggered the latest execution.
  • When defining an advanced action flow that calls APIs in external systems, you must authenticate the connection as required by the system. This could be through a registered OAuth connection or providing an API key or bearer token that is stored as an encrypted Secret within the workflow. It is also possible to use APIs that have no authentication requirements.
  • Zendesk API access is deny-by-default against an allowlist. Advanced action flows run with the permissions and account rate limits associated with the admin who created the workflow.
  • Local variables don't persist through pause steps in advanced action flows. Any variables needed after a pause step must be in storage.

Understanding advanced action flow limits

The following execution limits are enforced by Zendesk. Exceeding these limits results in runtime errors that are recorded in the execution trace.

Execution limits

Limit Value
Execution timeout Default of 5 minutes, but can be configured between 1 second and 10 minutes.

pause() isn't counted aggainst the execution timeout, but sleep() is counted.
Memory 128 MB per execution
Maximum pause duration 30 days
Concurrent HTTP requests within one execution 8
Concurrent AI steps within one execution 4
Recorded operations per execution 100,000
Automatic retries on failed requests Up to 5 for server errors and rate-limit responses

Data size limits

Limit Value
Flow output 2 MB
HTTP request body 48 MB
agent.run() text input 20 KiB

articles.name: How can I add a hyperlink or image to my signature?
articles.title: How can I add a hyperlink or image to my signature?
articles.body:
Question

How do I customize my signature with hyperlinks and images? Can I use a locally saved image in my signature?

Answer

No. You can't use an image saved locally on your computer in your agent signature.

To use an image in your signature, upload the file to a public image hosting site or save it as an asset in your knowledge base. This process generates a public URL that you can use in the Markdown code for your signature.

You can use Markdown formatting to add images and hyperlinks to your signature.

To add a hyperlink in Support:

  1. Click your avatar at the top right corner and then select Manage profile. 

  2. Under Signature on the left-hand panel, type the Markdown text below.

    [Link display text]
(https://www.zendesk.com)


Alternatively, add an image that is also a link using this Markdown:

[![alttext](imageurl)](linkurl)
  • Replace linkurl with the link for the image to direct toward
  • Replace imageurl with the link to the hosted image. After you resize the image, use an image host such as imgur.com > Wait five seconds for the image to load > Right-click the image > Select Copy image link. This returns the link to paste instead of imageurl

To display the image without a clickable link, use this Markdown:

![](imageurl)

This functionality also applies to global and brand signatures.

Tip: Use a PNG or JPEG file and size the image to a smaller size, between 5 KB to 50 KB. For optimal display, start with an image size of approximately 120px wide by 40px high. Adjust as needed to maintain the logo proportions. Ensure the image is on an HTTPS server and test the signature in email clients and the Agent Workspace to ensure proper display.

articles.name: A conversation displays an automated resolution but it was escalated to an agent
articles.title: A conversation displays an automated resolution but it was escalated to an agent
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

A conversation in an email escalated to an agent, but it shows an automated resolution. An escalation shouldn’t be an automated resolution. What happened?

Resolution steps

From your description of the behavior, the conversation isn’t an email interaction. It’s a messaging conversation, handled by the AI agent.

The AI agent attempted to escalate the conversation to a human agent, but no agents were available to accept the handoff. For this reason, the escalation couldn't complete. Instead, the bot created a ticket for follow-up and then finished the conversation itself.

This explains why you see both elements:

  • Custom resolution: Escalated to agent — because the bot reached the escalation step and attempted the handoff
  • Conversation status: Automated resolution — because no human agent actually joined the live messaging conversation, so it ended with the bot

While labels can look contradictory at first, labels describe two different parts of the same flow. In this case, it appears to be a failed handoff or no-agents-available scenario in messaging, rather than an email case or a successful live escalation to an agent.

articles.title: Can I prioritize the use case resolution with AI agents and emails?
articles.body:
Question

With a double intent in emails with an AI agent, can we prioritize the order of my use case resolutions?

Answer

No, there isn't a way to prioritize the resolution with more than one or multiple use cases.

  • The AI agent will try to solve as many use cases as your settings allow.
  • In addition, the AI agent will only start the next use case if the customer asks for it.

If you want to change the phone number in the user's profile, you can also use this method to update the user's phone number.

articles.name: Announcing endpoint changes for the Ultimate Public API
articles.title: Announcing endpoint changes for the Ultimate Public API
articles.body:
As part of our commitment to improving the stability and performance of our AI services, Zendesk is migrating Ultimate Public API services to the Zendesk Operating System (ZOS). This migration ensures a more unified experience and better integration with your existing Zendesk infrastructure.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Zendesk is updating the endpoints for the Ultimate Public API. Effective immediately, you must update your API endpoints from the legacy Ultimate domain to your dedicated Zendesk subdomain. 

  • Legacy URL structure: *.ultimate.ai
  • New URL structure: <yoursubdomain>.zendesk.com/ai-agents/api

These new endpoints are required for continued use of the Public API following the migration to the Zendesk Operating System.

Note: This change applies to Public API requests. It excludes default automatic webhooks, which Zendesk will migrate automatically. Custom webhooks may still require manual updates. See Webhook migration details below.

For more information, see AI Agents in our developer documentation.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

This update is a key preparation step for our broader platform migration to ZOS. By transitioning to Zendesk-hosted endpoints, we can deliver:

  • Seamless routing: Direct integration within your existing Zendesk infrastructure.
  • Minimal service disruption: Standardized routing through the Zendesk edge network layer.
  • Enhanced scalability and security: Improved overall system performance and protection for your AI agents.

Updating your endpoints ahead of time ensures that your custom integrations remain operational, reliable, and performant once the ZOS migration completes.

What do I need to do?

To avoid service interruptions, you must update your API configurations to point to the new Zendesk endpoints by September 15, 2026. 

  1. Identify all applications, scripts, and webhooks making requests to *.ultimate.ai.
  2. Replace *.ultimate.ai with your account-specific Zendesk URL format: <yoursubdomain>.zendesk.com/ai-agents/
  3. Test your endpoints in a sandbox or non-production environment prior to the deadline.

If these changes are not completed by September 15, 2026, you will be unable to use the Public API post-migration.

Webhook migration details

Zendesk will automatically migrate the default Ultimate automation webhook that was created during your bot setup. No action is required for this default webhook.

In Zendesk, this webhook is typically named Ultimate.ai Automation Webhook: <botId>

The webhook name can be changed, so the name alone may not always identify it. The default webhook is the one associated with the bot configuration created during setup.

Only the default webhook created as part of the bot setup is automatically migrated. Any other customer-created or custom-configured webhooks should be reviewed to ensure they use the appropriate new Zendesk URL structure.

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Service Incident - August 13, 2026 - Sunshine Platform, Support, Analytics, Sales | Pods 28 & 29 - No Healthy Upstream responses on multiple Zendesk services
articles.title: Service Incident - August 13, 2026 - Sunshine Platform, Support, Analytics, Sales | Pods 28 & 29 - No Healthy Upstream responses on multiple Zendesk services
articles.body:
Summary

On August 13, 2026, from 15:14 UTC to 16:38 UTC, customers on Pods 28 and 29 experienced elevated HTTP 500 and 503 errors, resulting in degraded or unavailable functionality across Sell, Explore, Sunshine Conversations, Support/Support SDK, Interaction History, and the Events API.

Timeline

August 13, 2026 4:06 UTC | August 13, 2026 9:06 AM PT

We are receiving reports of an issue affecting pods 28 and 29 that is causing impact to multiple products, including Sell and Explore, returning errors. We are investigating and will provide further details shortly.
Thank you for your patience in the meantime.

August 13, 2026 4:21 UTC | August 13, 2026 9:21 AM PT

We have confirmed an issue affecting multiple products on pods 28 and 29, including Explore, Sales, Sunshine Conversations, and Support/Support SDK. Our team is working to mitigate the impact and we will provide additional information when we have a substantive update to share. 
Thank you for your patience in the meantime.

August 13, 2026 4:43 UTC | August 13, 2026 9:43 AM PT

We are beginning to see recovery from the issue affecting multiple products on pods 28 and 29. We will monitor the situation to ensure full recovery across all products. Please let us know if you continue to experience any issues.

August 13, 2026 5:03 UTC | August 2, 2026 10:03 PM PT

Thank you for your patience while we resolved the issue impacting multiple Zendesk products in pod 28 and 29. We have observed full recovery across all the impacted products.

Root Cause Analysis

This incident was caused by an infrastructure rollback that inadvertently removed required DNS configuration for Pods 28 and 29. This prevented services from resolving and communicating with dependencies across pods, resulting in service connectivity failures and elevated error rates.

Resolution

To fix the issue, our engineers manually re-associated the required private domain settings with the virtual networks for Pods 29 and 28. We then conducted thorough validation steps to ensure that these associations were correctly reinstated across all affected pods, thereby restoring proper service communication.

Remediation Items

  1. Improve record retention so important operational information remains available during extended service delays.
  2. Add early warnings when required service connectivity is not configured correctly.
  3. Automate configuration management and ensure changes can be safely undone if needed.
  4. Define clear responsibility for shared connectivity settings across teams.
  5. Strengthen monitoring to detect service communication issues sooner and reduce the time needed to respond.

FOR MORE INFORMATION

For current system status information about Zendesk and specific impacts to your account, visit our system status page. If you have additional questions about this incident, contact Zendesk customer support.

articles.name: Using the conversation simulator to test your AI agents (EAP)
articles.title: Using the conversation simulator to test your AI agents (EAP)
articles.body:
The AI agent conversation simulator generates realistic customer conversations based on scenarios you create. It's a great way to test your AI agents before you deploy them.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise
This feature is currently in an Early Access Program (EAP). If you want to test out the conversation simulator, see Signing up for the EAP below.

The AI agent conversation simulator generates realistic customer conversations based on scenarios you create. It's a great way to test your AI agents before you deploy them.

The conversation simulator allows you to:
  • Run multi-turn conversations against live AI agent configurations
  • Estimate automated resolution rates and conversation quality
  • Provide a results dashboard to help you analyse results

Simulated conversations are generated from a customer profile and a scenario that you define, or you can have AI generate them from a prompt you supply.

Note: You must use the conversation simulator with a messaging AI agent. It's not compatible with other AI agent types.

This article contains the following topics:

  • Signing up for the EAP
  • Creating customer profiles
  • Creating scenarios
  • Running a scenario
  • Reviewing your results
  • Managing customer profiles and scenarios
  • Managing run results
  • Example scenarios and customer profiles

Signing up for the EAP

Before you can use the conversation simulator EAP, you must activate it in Admin Center.

To sign up for the EAP

  1. In Admin Center, click Account in the sidebar, then select Early Access Programs > Experiments.
  2. From the list of Early Access Programs, select Conversation Simulator.

The EAP is now active in your account.

Creating customer profiles

Customer profiles give the conversation simulator details of a fictional customer. You can create a customer profile manually, or have AI create it for you. Customer profiles you create can be used by any of your scenarios. You must create at least one customer profile to use the conversation simulator.

The AI agent conversation simulator is designed for testing with fictional data. Avoid using real customer names, email addresses, or other personal information.

Creating a customer profile using AI

If you don't want to manually create the customer profile, you can create it using AI based on a prompt you enter.

To create a customer profile using AI

  1. On the AI agents workspace home page () , select the AI agent you want to test against. The agent you select must be a messaging AI agent.
  2. Click Test in the sidebar.
  3. Click the Customer profiles tab.

    The Customer profiles page displays all of your current customer profiles. You can sort the list by alphabetical order, last updated date, and newest or oldest first.

  4. Click New profile.
  5. In the Generate with AI panel, enter text to define the customer. For example, "A short-tempered, curt customer with a limited knowledge of computers".
  6. Click Generate.

    The conversation simulator completes all fields on the page.

  7. Review the values that were generated and then click Save. Your customer profile is created and appears in the list of customer profiles.

Creating a customer profile manually

If you want full control over your customer profile details, create the profile manually.

To manually create a customer profile

  1. In the AI agents workspace, click Test in the sidebar.
  2. Click the Customer profiles tab.

    The Customer profiles page displays all of your current customer profiles. You can sort the list by alphabetical order, last updated date, and newest or oldest first.

  3. Click New profile.
  4. Configure the following:
    1. Configure the following:
      • Name: Enter a short descriptive name for the customer profile such as "Curt tech novice."
      • Description: Enter a detailed description of the customer's personality, background, and behavior. See Example scenarios and customer profiles for examples to get you started.
      • Mock values: Mock values are fictional key-value pairs that give a simulated conversation consistent facts about the customer, account, order, or scenario state. They help you test specific conditions repeatedly and safely without using real customer data. They are referred to by either the customer or agent when dealing with a relevant scenario as a way to simulate how a real conversation might happen about the same problem. Enter key-value pairs to use in the simulation, for example:
        • Customer_name - John Smith
        • Account_status - Active

        Click Add mock value to add more key-value pairs.

      • Tags: Enter one or more tags to help you categorize and find the customer scenario you want.
  5. Click Save.

    Your customer profile is created and appears in the list of customer profiles.

Creating scenarios

Scenarios define a business situation that can be used for a simulated conversation. For example, a customer might be struggling to apply a promo code or cannot access a dashboard. You can choose from several prebuilt scenarios, or you can create your own. The Scenarios tab is where you can view, create, and manage your scenarios.

Creating a scenario using AI

If you don't want to manually create the scenario, you can create it using AI based on a prompt you enter.

  1. In the AI agents workspace, click Test in the sidebar.
  2. Click the Scenarios tab.

    The Scenarios page displays all of your current scenarios. You can sort the list by alphabetical order, last updated date, and newest or oldest first.

  3. Click Create scenario.
  4. Configure the following:
    1. In the Generate scenario with AI panel, enter text to define the scenario. For example, "A frustrated customer who ordered a laptop received the wrong product."
    2. Click Generate.

      The conversation simulator completes all fields on the page.

  5. Click Save. Your scenario is created and appears in the list of customer profiles. Each time you edit a scenario, the conversation simulator creates a new version of the scenario.

Creating a scenario manually

If you want full control over your scenario details, create the scenario manually.

  1. In the AI agents workspace, click Test in the sidebar.
  2. Click the Scenarios tab.

    The Scenarios page displays all of your current scenarios. You can sort the list by alphabetical order, last updated date, and newest or oldest first.

    Tip: The conversation simulator includes several prebuilt scenarios you can use to save time. Click the Scenario library tab to see the available scenarios.
  3. Click Create scenario.
  4. Configure the following values. See Example scenarios and customer profiles for examples to get you started.
    • Scenario name: Enter a short descriptive name for the scenario such as "Wrong laptop delivered."
    • Background context: Provide further context about the scenario.
    • Initial problem: Detail the customer's main issue.
    • Expected outcome: Provide details about what the resolution should be for this problem.
    • Mock values: Mock values are fictional key-value pairs that give a simulated conversation consistent facts about the customer, account, order, or scenario state. They help you test specific conditions repeatedly and safely without using real customer data. They are referred to by either the customer or agent when dealing with a relevant scenario as a way to simulate how a real conversation might happen about the same problem. Enter key-value pairs to use in the simulation, for example:
      • Customer_name - John Smith
      • Account_status - Active

      Click Add mock value to add more key-value pairs.

    • Tags: Enter one or more tags to help you categorize and find the customer scenario you want.
  5. Click Save. Your scenario is created and appears in the list of scenarios. Each time you edit a scenario, the conversation simulator creates a new version of the scenario.

Using a prebuilt scenario

You can select from several prebuilt scenarios instead of creating a new one. These scenarios are available to all users. You can copy these scenarios to your personal list and edit them as required. Some scenarios might contain actions that are not compatible with the chosen agent, causing the conversation to fail.

To use a prebuilt scenario

  1. In the AI agents workspace, click Test in the sidebar.
  2. Click the Scenario library tab.

    The Scenario library page displays the available prebuilt scenarios.

  3. Click the scenario you want to use.
  4. Select one of the following options:
    • Use this scenario: Selects the scenario and opens its' page where you can run it.
    • Edit scenario: Opens the scenario page where you can make changes to the prebuilt scenario and save it to your personal scenarios.
    • Cancel: Takes no action and returns you to the scenario library page.

Running a scenario

Once you have a customer profile and a scenario, you can generate a simulated conversation.

To run a scenario

  1. In the AI agents workspace, click Test in the sidebar.
  2. Click the Scenarios tab.
  3. On the scenario page, click the scenario you want to test.
  4. Provide the following information:
    • Customer profile: Select the customer profile to run or click New profile to create a new one.
    • Scenario version: Select the version you want to run, if you've saved multiple versions of your scenario.
    • Conversations: Configure the number of conversations you want to generate in this run.

  5. Click Run.

Reviewing your results

After the conversation simulator runs, it displays the status of each simulated conversation. If you configured more than one conversation, each of these displays separately.

To view your results

  1. Click a conversation to open the results.

  2. The results show the background, customer profile, expected outcome, and mock values you configured. Below this the simulated conversation is displayed. You can click Show details to view all of the steps and logic used by the conversation simulator when generating the results.

Managing customer profiles and scenarios

After you've created a customer profile and scenario, there are several actions you can take to manage it.

To manage customer profiles and scenarios

  • In the AI agents workspace, click Test in the sidebar.
  • Click the Customer profiles tab or the Scenarios tab.
  • Beside the scenario or customer profile you want to manage, click the options menu (), then choose one of the following actions:
    • Open: (Scenarios only) Opens the scenario run page where you can start a test run.
    • Edit: Opens the scenario or customer profile for editing.
    • Delete: Deletes the selected scenario or customer profile.

Managing run results

The following actions can be taken on any of your generated conversations:

  • Deletes the selected conversation.
  • Exports the selected conversation in JSON format. You can find the exported conversation in your Downloads folder.
  • Click the Runs history tab on the Scenarios page to see the status of any previous runs.

Example scenarios and customer profiles

In this section, you'll find an example scenario and customer profile to get you started. Feel free to change these to suit your business needs.

Example scenario

Every scenario contains the following sections. Use these examples as a starting point for creating your own scenarios:

  • Background context: "TechNova Electronics is a mid-size online retailer of consumer electronics. Standard policy allows a 30-day exchange/return window, free return shipping if the wrong item was sent or if the item is defective, and a replacement shipment of the exact model when available. The incident occurred after a recent order placed on 2026-07-28 for a LAP-XYZ Pro 15 laptop. The customer received a different model (wrong product) on delivery 2026-08-01 and contacted customer support on 2026-08-03. The case requires verification of shipment details, identification of the error in fulfillment, and coordination of an immediate replacement with a prepaid return for the incorrect item. Stock availability for the correct model is confirmed, and the agent should guide the customer through the exchange process, including shipping timelines and any necessary pickup arrangements."
  • Initial problem: "Customer reports receiving the wrong laptop: they ordered LAP-XYZ Pro 15 (SKU-LAP-XYZ15) but the package contained LAP-ABC 13 (SKU-LAP-ABC13). The customer is frustrated due to the mix-up and delay, and requests the correct laptop to be shipped immediately, with a prepaid label to return the incorrect item. They also want clear tracking information and assurance that no extra charges will be incurred."
  • Expected outcome: "Replace with the correct LAP-XYZ Pro 15 laptop at no cost, shipped with expedited delivery, plus a prepaid return label for the incorrect LAP-ABC 13. Provide a prepaid pickup or drop-off option for the wrong item, send updated tracking for the replacement, and confirm the exchange will be completed within 3-5 business days if possible. If the replacement cannot be fulfilled quickly, offer a full refund and arrange return pickup. Communicate next steps, timelines, and any required confirmations."

Example customer profile

"A short-tempered, curt customer with a limited understanding of computers. They speak in brief, clipped sentences and expect quick, definite answers. They become frustrated easily when explanations are long, use jargon, or require multiple steps. They prefer direct, step-by-step instructions and concrete actions they can perform themselves without deep technical detail. They respond poorly to salesy or overly friendly language, and may react defensively if they feel talked down to. They are more comfortable with everyday apps than with advanced settings; they can follow basic troubleshooting cues but need simple, verifiable checks. They generally remain focused on resolving issues quickly, though their mood can swing toward impatience if progress stalls. Communication style: blunt, sometimes sarcastic, often uses imperative phrases like 'What do I click next?' They value efficiency, clarity, and tangible results, and may push back on back-and-forth troubleshooting that doesn't seem to lead to a solution. They appreciate calm, patient guidance and quick confirmation when a step has worked."

articles.name: Parameters are missing in an API Order Status use case
articles.title: Parameters are missing in an API Order Status use case
articles.body:
Issue symptoms

When using an API Order Status use case, some parameter values may appear in the API call configuration but fail to populate during the conversation. In some cases, only one parameter is collected while the remaining required values are missing, which prevents the order status workflow from triggering correctly.

Resolution steps

A common cause is that multiple API integrations were created for the same Order Status check. If one of those integrations requires more parameters than the bot collects in the Order Status use case, the workflow may fail and only some values may populate. Misconfigured or missing API parameters can also contribute to the issue.

To resolve the issue:

  • Review the API integrations configured for the same Order Status check
  • Remove any duplicate API integration that is conflicting with the intended setup
  • Confirm that the remaining API integration includes the correct required parameters
  • Verify that the bot is collecting every parameter needed by the Order Status use case
  • Test the flow again to confirm that all parameter values populate and the API triggers successfully

If the issue was caused by a duplicate integration requiring additional parameters, deleting that duplicate integration should allow the correct values to populate as expected.

To learn more API integrations in AI agents, see About the integration builder for AI agents.

articles.name: Converting tickets to service requests
articles.title: Converting tickets to service requests
articles.body:
When the service catalog is turned on for a brand, agents can convert tickets into service requests when they are associated with a service catalog item. When a service is set for a ticket, the ticket's form, fields, and requirements are updated to the applicable service request form. This allows agents to convert requests received through other channels, such as email or web form, into service requests.

What's my plan?
All Suites Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

When the service catalog is turned on for a brand, agents can convert tickets into service requests when they are associated with a service catalog item. When a service is set for a ticket, the ticket's form, fields, and requirements are updated to the applicable service request form. This allows agents to convert requests received through other channels, such as email or web form, into service requests.

This article contains the following topics:
  • Considerations when converting tickets to service requests
  • Converting tickets to service requests
  • Converting a service request to a ticket
Related articles:
  • Adding services to your service catalog
  • Submitting service catalog requests

Considerations when converting tickets to service requests

All tickets associated with brand that has a service catalog turned on include a Service ticket field. Requests submitted through the service catalog are automatically created with a service request form, but requests submitted through other channels use ticket forms by default. Adding a value to a ticket's service field, either manually or with a business rule, converts a ticket to a service request.

When the ticket form changes to a service request form associated with the selected service, the following things happen:
  • The ticket displays the fields configured for the selected service.
  • Values are retained for fields that are present on both forms.
  • Required fields on the service request form must be completed before the ticket can be saved.

A service request can be converted to a ticket by removing the value in the service field.

You can't convert closed requests from tickets to service requests or vice versa.

Converting tickets to service requests

Tickets are converted to service requests by adding a value to the ticket's service field. This can be done automatically, with triggers, or manually by agents. See:
  • Automatically adding a service to a ticket
  • Manually adding a service to a ticket

Automatically adding a service to a ticket

To use triggers to automatically add a service to a ticket, use the Service > Service action.

To automatically add a service to a ticket
  1. Create or edit a ticket trigger.
  2. Under Conditions, specify one or more qualifications the ticket must meet to be converted to a service request.
  3. Under Actions, click Add action and select: Service > Service | Service catalog item, where Service catalog item is replaced with a service from your service catalog.

    The the service specified in the action statement's Value field is the value that is added to the ticket's Service field.

Manually adding a service to a ticket

If an agent is working a ticket and determines it needs to be converted to a service request, they can manually add the service to the ticket as long as it has a status of new, open, pending, or on-hold.

To manually add a service to a ticket
  1. In Support, access a ticket.
  2. In the ticket properties panel, under Service, select the service being requested in the ticket.
  3. Review the fields on the service request form to ensure all required fields contain values.
  4. Save your change by clicking Submit as and selecting the appropriate status.

Converting a service request to a ticket

Deselecting a service from a ticket's service field removes the association between a ticket and the service catalog item and converts it back to a ticket form.

To manually remove a ticket's service value
  1. In Support, access a ticket and set the Service field to an empty value.
  2. Save your change by clicking Submit as and selecting the appropriate status.

articles.name: Linking directly to comments in a ticket
articles.title: Linking directly to comments in a ticket
articles.body:
As an agent, you often need to reference a specific update, decision, or customer reply in a long ticket conversation. You can create links to connect directly to specific comments within a ticket and share it with others. Comment links make it easier to share the exact context with teammates, collaborate on complex requests, and reduce the time spent searching through ticket histories.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus
Support Team, Professional, or Enterprise

As an agent, you often need to reference a specific update, decision, or customer reply in a long ticket conversation. You can create links to connect directly to specific comments within a ticket and share it with others. Comment links make it easier to share the exact context with teammates, collaborate on complex requests, and reduce the time spent searching through ticket histories.

This article contains the following sections:

  • About ticket comment links
  • Creating and sharing ticket comment links

Related articles:

  • Adding comments to tickets

About ticket comment links

Using a Copy link option within a ticket, you can copy a direct link to a specific ticket comment and share it with others. When someone clicks the link, the link opens the ticket, navigates to the referenced comment, and highlights it for easy reference.

Comment links follow Zendesk’s existing ticket access permissions:

  • Users can access a linked comment only if they have permission to access the ticket.
  • Sharing a link does not grant additional access to a ticket or its comments.
  • Redacted comments remain linkable and can still be located in a ticket.
  • If a linked comment has been deleted or is no longer available, Zendesk will handle the link without exposing unavailable content.

Typical uses for sharing comment links include:

  • References from one ticket to another
  • Links shared within the same ticket conversation
  • Slack or other internal messaging tools
  • Emails
  • Documentation tools such as Google Docs
  • Internal notes or collaboration workflows

The Copy link option is available for comments in:

  • Tickets from all channels, except Chat.
  • Tickets that aren't archived.
  • Tickets created on or after January 1, 2026

Creating and sharing ticket comment links

To share ticket comments links, you can copy the link directly from a ticket comment and paste the link into another document, another ticket, or another location within the same ticket.

To create and share a comment link

  1. In a ticket, locate the comment you want to share.
  2. Click the options menu icon () next to the comment.

  3. Select Copy link from the options menu.

    The comment link is copied to your clipboard and you’ll see a confirmation message.

  4. Paste the link into another location, wherever you want to include the ticket comment link.

To open a comment link
  • Click the comment link.

    The link opens the associated ticket in Support, scrolls to the referenced comment, and highlights it.

articles.name: Workflow: Capture a customer’s name and email in an AI agent and sync it to Zendesk tickets
articles.title: Workflow: Capture a customer’s name and email in an AI agent and sync it to Zendesk tickets
articles.body:
AI agents can collect a customer's name and email during a messaging conversation and pass that information to Zendesk when a ticket is created. This is useful when customers start a conversation as anonymous users and you want the resulting ticket to include their details.

This article provides two workflow options:

  • Collect customer details with a customer message block
  • Collect customer details with a form in an AI agent message

In both workflows, you use an Update user action to write the customer's name and email to the Sunshine Conversations user profile before the ticket is created.

Before you start

Before setting up this workflow, make sure that:

  • You're using an AI agent with messaging
  • You have permission to create or edit AI agent flows and actions
  • You understand your account's messaging email identity settings

If you want to associate messaging users with existing Zendesk users before the conversation starts, you also need end-user authentication for messaging using JWT, which requires developer implementation.

Option 1: Use a customer message block

Step 1: Add message blocks to collect the customer's name and email

Add customer message blocks in the flow before the escalation step. Use one block to ask for the customer's name and another to ask for the customer's email address.

Configure each block to save the customer response as a parameter so you can reuse the values later in the flow.

Example:

  • Ask for the customer's name and save it to a parameter such as name
  • Ask for the customer's email address and save it to a parameter such as email

After the values are collected, reference them in later blocks using the parameter format:

  • {{name}}
  • {{email}}

Step 2: Pass the saved values during escalation

When the flow reaches the escalation path or a specific downstream block, create an action and pass the saved parameter values using the parameter formats {{name}} and {{email}}.

Using the double angle bracket {{}} format ensures the stored parameter values are passed correctly.

Option 2: Use a form in an AI agent message

Step 1: Add a form to the AI agent message

Create or select a form template that collects the customer's name and email, then add that form to your AI agent message.

Add the form template to connect it to the relevant flow or escalation path.

Step 2: Verify the parameter names

Then run a test conversation and review the session data to confirm the exact parameter names created by the form. Check the conversation log for the test conversation and review the session parameters ensuring they are set from the template form.

Step 3: Create an Update user action

Create an action for Sunshine Conversations that updates the user profile.

Map the form's saved parameter values to these user fields:

  • givenName = {{name}}
  • email = {{customerEmail}}

The parameter names in the action must exactly match the ones saved by the form.

Step 4: Add the action with the Escalation

Add the Update user action in the escalation block or in the relevant AI agent configuration so it runs before the ticket is created.

This links the collected form details to the Sunshine Conversations user profile before the ticket is generated.

Understand how email identity settings affect the ticket requester

Whether the collected email appears on the Zendesk ticket depends on your messaging email identity settings.

  • If your account allows unverified emails, the email collected by the AI agent can be added as a user identity and used as the ticket requester
  • If your account allows only verified emails, the collected email won't be used as a trusted identity unless the user is authenticated and the email is verified
  • In unauthenticated conversations where only verified emails are allowed, the ticket may appear as a conversation with a web user instead of showing the collected email address

To learn more about email identities see Understanding and setting up end-user authentication for messaging.

If you want to identify customers against existing user profiles before the conversation starts, use JWT-based end-user authentication for messaging. This requires developer implementation or help from Zendesk Professional Services.

Issue symptoms

In the new dashboard builder, you can't select Publish changes from the dropdown menu after you edit a report.

To fix the issue:

  1. Open the Dashboard in Edit mode
  2. Make a minor change, for example, resize a widget or change a widget color
  3. Verify that Publish changes becomes active
  4. Click Publish changes to save and publish

articles.name: Announcing the EAP for AI-powered action flow creation through admin copilot
articles.title: Announcing the EAP for AI-powered action flow creation through admin copilot
articles.body:
Zendesk is excited to announce the early access program (EAP) for AI-powered action flow creation with admin copilot. This feature lets admins generate complete, production-ready action flows using plain-language prompts in admin copilot. No coding or deep technical expertise required.

This announcement includes the following topics:

  • What is changing?
  • Why is Zendesk making this change?
  • What do I need to do?

What is changing?

Admin copilot can now generate entire action flows from a natural-language description. Simply describe what you want to automate, and the AI builds the flow, including triggers, first-party Zendesk actions, third-party connector steps, custom actions, and custom code steps, directly in the action builder. You can then review, edit, test, and activate the flow without writing a single line of code.

Key capabilities included in this EAP:

  • Prompt-to-flow generation: Describe your use case in plain language (in English or your local language) and admin copilot generates a complete, visualized workflow.
  • Starter prompts: Six pre-defined prompts are surfaced in admin copilot to help you quickly build common automation scenarios.
  • Fully editable: Every generated flow is fully editable in the action builder. You can modify steps, swap out connectors, or adjust logic before activating.
  • AI-assisted custom code: Need a data transformation step? Admin copilot can generate the JavaScript for custom code steps from a plain-language description. No JavaScript experience needed.
  • Error diagnosis and remediation: If a generated flow contains errors, you can send them directly to admin copilot for automated troubleshooting and fix suggestions.
  • Third-party connection handling: If a flow requires a third-party system you haven't connected yet, admin copilot seamlessly prompts you to complete the authentication step. 
  • Edit existing flows: Open an existing action flow and use prompts to modify steps, add new steps, or restructure logic.

Example flows you can generate:

  • Auto-escalate urgent tickets: Detect urgency signals in ticket content and notify the on-call team in Slack.
  • Ticket routing: Auto-assign tickets based on skills, language, or priority; escalate if CSAT rating is negative and notify a Slack channel
  • Log negative CSAT to a sheet and alert manager: Automatically log poor customer ratings to a Google Sheet for tracking and alert team leads in Slack.
  • Merge duplicate tickets by reference: Search for incoming tickets sharing the same reference ID and merge newer tickets into the existing thread.

Known limitations

  • Custom code steps can only be used for data transformation. They cannot make network calls or invoke Zendesk APIs not natively available in action builder, such as reading ticket attachments or comments.
  • AI-generated flows might require manual adjustment to match your specific account configuration before activation.
  • Third-party connections not yet set up in your account will require a one-time authentication step prompted by admin copilot.

Why is Zendesk making this change?

Building action flows today requires technical knowledge, and frequently requires admins to work with developers and IT resources to build and maintain the automated workflows. Complex flows with 10 or more steps are time-consuming to build in the UI, which slows adoption and leaves automation potential untapped.

Admin copilot removes the blank-canvas barrier. Whether you're automating a ticket routing rule, an employee off-boarding process, or an inventory restock workflow, you can now describe what you need and have a working flow ready to review in seconds.

What do I need to do?

This EAP is open to all eligible customers across Zendesk Suite Professional plans and above, which have access to both action builder and admin copilot. 

If you're interested in participating in this EAP, turn on the EAP from the Action flows page in Admin Center or contact your Zendesk account representative.After joining, the AI-powered flow generation capability is automatically available on the Action flows page and admin copilot interface, complete with starter prompts to help you begin. See Using AI to generate action flows (EAP).

Your feedback during EAP is critical to shaping this feature before general availability. Please share your experience including what worked, what didn't, and what use cases you'd like to see supported. 

If you have feedback or questions related to this announcement, visit our community forum where we collect and manage customer product feedback. For general assistance with your Zendesk products, contact Zendesk Customer Support.

articles.name: Using live call transcripts in Zendesk Talk
articles.title: Using live call transcripts in Zendesk Talk
articles.body:
You can use the transcript to review what has been said and search for details to check information during the call without interrupting the conversation. You can also use real-time suggestions during the call, seeUsing real-time AI suggestions for voice calls.

What's my plan?
All Suites Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus

Summary: ◀▼

Live call transcription gives you a real-time text transcript during voice calls, with speaker labels, timestamps, and auto-scrolling updates. You can review what’s been said, search for keywords or phrases, switch transcription language during the call, and check details without interrupting the customer. It also supports multilingual transcription for common languages.

Zendesk Suite customers must also have the Copilot add-on to use this feature.
If your admin has turned on live call transcription, you have access to a real-time text version of a voice call while the conversation is in progress. The transcript shows speaker labels (Agent or Customer), timestamps from the start of the call, and automatically scrolls to show the most recent conversation.

You can use the transcript to review what has been said and search for details to check information during the call without interrupting the conversation. You can also use real-time suggestions during the call, see Using real-time AI suggestions for voice calls.

To use live transcripts during an ongoing call

  1. In the ticket call controls, click Show transcript ().

    The transcript panel opens in the ticket, below the controls, showing the most recent part of the conversation and updates automatically as the conversation continues.

  2. Click the expand icon (v) in the upper-right corner of the transcript panel to access the whole conversation.

    The transcript auto-scrolls to show the latest conversation.
  3. (Optional) Scroll up and down to review the whole conversation.
  4. (Optional) Click Scroll to latest at the bottom of the panel to access the current conversation.

  5. To find a specific topic, search in the upper-right corner of the transcript panel and enter a keyword or phrase.

    It's a case-insensitive search that supports partial matches. This allows you to jump to relevant parts of the conversation and check specific details. For example, information about an "account", "order" or "error message".

    The transcript highlights all instances of the search term. If there are multiple matches, use the arrows to move between matches.

  6. (Optional) In the language menu, select the language you want to use for transcription.

    The transcript language defaults to your Zendesk profile language. You can change the language during an active call to match the language the customer is speaking. The transcript uses the new language for ongoing transcription. Previously transcribed text is not retranscribed.

    You can also select the multilingual language option to seamlessly switch between the following languages only: English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Russian, Portuguese, Japanese, Italian, and Dutch.

  7. Click Hide transcript () to close the transcript panel.

    Ending the call also closes the transcript panel.
